# What are the Advantages of Root Canal Treatment?

Dec 01, 2021

Dental patients have worries that root canals will be painful–but modern technologies, anesthesia options, and painkillers make root canal treatment much easier than ever before. Our dentists are twice as likely to recommend [**root canal treatment in Omaha, NE**](https://andingfamilydental.com/service/root-canal/), over tooth extraction.

Even though it is pain-free, it is vital to understand the benefits of a root canal procedure before deciding on getting the procedure.

## What is a Root Canal?

Root canal treatment is a surgical procedure that removes the infected pulp around the end of a tooth and replaces it with a filling. It can be performed as an outpatient procedure, and patients should experience minimal discomfort.

Root canals are not pleasant to think about, but they are necessary to save your teeth from further damage. If you experience tooth pain that lasts for more than two weeks, you should contact a dentist near you for an appointment.

## What are the Benefits of Root Canal Treatment?

Root canal treatment has multiple benefits, including:

1. It stops the spread of infectionA root canal is a treatment for a tooth infection. To prevent the spread of infection, the dentist will remove the infected tooth and clean it thoroughly.After the root canal treatment, the dentist will fill it up with a temporary filling material that fits within them. The holes are sealed with a permanent filling material after a few weeks.The root canal stops the infection from spreading by removing bacteria-containing debris from inside your tooth and sealing off its entrance ways into your body.
2. It Prevents Tooth ExtractionA root canal is a procedure that removes diseased tissue in the center of your root. It helps to prevent the need for extraction.Tooth extraction is a dental problem, and it can lead to other problems like bone deterioration.A root canal procedure removes the infected pulp and seals off the teeth. This will stop the spread of infection and tooth damage. Remember, tooth extraction is not a reversible procedure, and you will rely on other restorative procedures to replace your teeth.
3. It is a pain-free procedureMany patients prefer root canals over extractions because they are a more predictable treatment. They typically only require a day or two of recovery instead of weeks. Additionally, root canals are painless and have no discomfort during recovery.Root canals are generally painless as they don’t involve tearing or cutting the gum tissue; this means that patients should not experience post-operative discomfort or problems chewing soft foods for at least four weeks after treatment.
4. It offers a visually appealing resultThe final step of the root canal treatment is fixing dental crowns. These are caps that cover the teeth to restore the strength of the teeth and also their appearance. Although the crowns are available in different materials, the porcelain crowns are often used because they resemble your teeth.

## What are the Risks of Not Getting a Root Canal Treatment?

The risk of not getting one is that it can lead to more serious dental problems, which will require much more expensive treatments down the line.

## What Happens When You Get a Root Canal?

Because it can be a painful and lengthy procedure, many people avoid getting a root canal. But, people need to know what happens during this complicated dental surgery.

The dentist will clean out the infected tooth before drilling into the cavity or pulp chamber. Once this has been done, he will drill into the center of where the infection is located using a surgical-grade instrument.

A bio-compatible material is used to fill the teeth and seal them. A temporary filling is also used as the dental crown is crafted.

You may experience discomfort, swelling, and pain after the procedure. These dental issues will clear after a while. However, if swelling persists or you experience fever, visit an [**emergency dentist in Omaha**](https://andingfamilydental.com/) for assistance.

## What is the Root Canal Aftercare Tips?

Proper aftercare is required to hasten the healing process. You will need to gently brush, eat soft food that doesn’t require chewing, avoid acidic beverages or foods like coffee or orange juice, etc. Also, schedule regular cleanings with your dentist.

## What Precisely Is Root Canal Treatment?

It can prevent further tooth damage and general health problems.

Our teeth are structured uniquely. Aside from the visible outer part, other structures inside the teeth allow us to perform various dental functions. These structures are essential and can become infected if we don’t take good care of your dental health.

The root canals in our teeth accommodate the blood vessels, nerve tissues, and most importantly, the dental pulp, which is responsible for teeth growth and development in children. However, a diseased dental pulp or tissue needs to go to prevent unwanted health complications. That is when root canal therapy is necessary.

Although there are other dental treatments for teeth infections, a root canal is one of the best ways to preserve your natural tooth and keep you safe from further infections.

## Why Do I Need A Root Canal Therapy?

Your **[dentist in Omaha](https://andingfamilydental.com/)** can ask you to get a root canal treatment or endodontic treatment for various reasons. Let’s see what these are.

If you have a broken tooth or cracked, microbes that cause infection can quickly get into the tooth’s roots. That is because the outer layer protecting the inner tooth structure is no longer viable. Once the infection gets into the dental pulp, it can cause the following dental problems:

* Severe toothache
* Tooth sensitivity
* Swollen gums
* Bone death around the top of infected tooth’ root’s
* Pus between the gums

If you want to avoid these nasty dental issues, it’s best to get root canal treatment.

## Performing Root Canal Treatment

To get a root canal treatment, you can consult our dentist in 68132. **[Dr. Michelle Chang](https://andingfamilydental.com/doctor/dr-michelle-chang/)** will take you through all the processes for your root canal treatment.

Your dentist will check your mouth before treatment begins. This helps them determine the exact location of the infection and see if there are other essential issues to note. You should tell your dentist about your medical history and any drugs you are currently taking to be safe.

If you are deemed fit for the procedure, your dentist will begin by administering a local anesthetic to desensitize the area, thereby making you numb to any discomfort or pain. Hence, the procedure is a relatively painless one.

Next, your dentist would access the infected tooth’s root and take out the decayed dental pulp. After the decayed dental pulp and tissues are gone, your dentist would clean, fill and seal the area to prevent the site from getting reinfected.

You can expect your dentist to recommend a dental crown after the process is complete. That is because the tooth can become delicate after the dental pulp is gone. The dental pulp forms a form of support for the tooth. Although the ligament that connects the tooth to the bone can support the tooth, the tooth can become weak over time. Attaching a crown would help protect the tooth against future damages.

After the procedure, your dentist would also put you through the different ways to protect your teeth and prevent infections from getting into your tooth’ roots again.

Maintenance after a root canal is as vital as the procedure itself. If infections get into the tooth’ root again, you might get another root canal treatment. If the condition is too complicated, a tooth extraction (removal of the infected tooth from its socket) might be the last resort.

Practice good oral hygiene and visit your dentist regularly for dental checkups to prevent this.


Root canal treatment or endodontic treatment is an oral treatment that involves the extraction of infections from the tooth roots.

## Why Do I Need One?

A root canal procedure becomes necessary when the inside of the tooth becomes infected or decayed. The process needs several visits and the last step is to remove the temporary fillings and give the tooth a final touch by placing crown over it. The crown helps in restoring the strength of the treated tooth.

## Is the Treatment Painful?

The root canal procedure is not painful thanks to the advancement in technology. It’s a simple and painless procedure of filling the cavities and placing the crown over the tooth. It is most important to understand that root canal treatment doesn’t cause pain; it is done for providing you relief from the pain.

Q: What is the goal of restorative dentistry?
A: Restorative dentistry focuses on repairing or replacing damaged, decayed, or missing teeth to restore oral function, comfort, and appearance. Treatments are designed to help patients achieve a healthy, natural-looking smile.

Q: Which restorative services do you offer?
A: Our restorative dentistry services include tooth-colored fillings, dental crowns, bridges, and implant restorations. We create personalized treatment plans based on each patient's dental needs and goals.

Q: How long do dental restorations last?
A: The lifespan of a dental restoration depends on the type of treatment, oral hygiene habits, and routine dental care. With proper maintenance and regular checkups, many crowns and bridges can last 10 to 15 years or longer.

Q: Is restorative dental work covered by insurance?
A: Many dental insurance plans provide partial coverage for restorative procedures that are considered medically necessary. Our team can review your benefits and discuss available payment options before treatment begins.
